- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid bearish overcorrection.  
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply downward bias to short-term forecasts.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overbought overreaction.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast slightly; if below, increase slightly.  
- Forecast horizon > 10 days: model tends to underestimate true volatility — add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for longer horizons.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, –1, +1), model fails to capture momentum reversal — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment swing direction.
